out.corrected_sentence: Yesterday I went to the shop and I bought two loaves of bread.

corrections.explanation_it: Per il passato semplice si usa solo la forma passata del verbo (went), non l'ausiliare have con il participio in questo contesto.
Il verbo 'to buy' è irregolare. Il participio passato e il passato semplice sono 'bought'.
In inglese 'bread' è un nome non numerabile. Per indicare due unità si dice 'two loaves of bread'.

out.reply: That sounds like a productive trip! What did you make with the bread?

new_vocab.example: I bought a loaf of bread for the sandwiches.
I need to go grocery shopping this afternoon.

out.follow_up: Can you tell me what else you bought at the shop?

out.corrected_sentence: If I have time tomorrow, I will call you.

corrections.explanation_it: Nelle frasi ipotetiche di primo tipo (first conditional), dopo 'if' si usa il presente semplice, non il futuro.
Per esprimere una promessa o un'azione futura nella parte principale della frase, devi usare 'will'.

out.reply: That sounds like a good plan. What are you going to do if you have some free time tomorrow?

new_vocab.example: I like to read books in my free time.

out.follow_up: Can you try to say the corrected sentence again?

out.corrected_sentence: She has been working here for three years and she doesn't like it.

corrections.original: is working here from three years
corrections.corrected: has been working here for three years
corrections.explanation_it: Per azioni che iniziano nel passato e continuano nel presente si usa il Present Perfect Continuous. Inoltre, con i periodi di tempo si usa 'for' e non 'from'.
Con la terza persona singolare (she) si usa l'ausiliare 'does not' o 'doesn't'.

out.reply: I am sorry to hear that she is not happy with her job. Why do you think she doesn't like it?

new_vocab.example: She wants to quit her job next month.
Her new position is very stressful.

out.follow_up: Do you like your job or is it stressful too?

out.corrected_sentence: I'm interested in learning English because I want to find a better job.

corrections.explanation_it: Usa 'interested' (interessato) invece di 'interesting' (interessante) per descrivere come ti senti. Dopo la preposizione 'in' si usa la forma in -ing.
Dopo il verbo 'want' devi sempre usare l'infinito con 'to'.

out.reply: That is a great motivation! Learning English can definitely open many doors for your career.

new_vocab.example: Learning a new language can open doors to new jobs.
I want to improve my career path.

out.follow_up: What kind of job are you looking for?

out.corrected_sentence: I depend on my parents for money.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese si usa la preposizione 'on' dopo il verbo 'depend', non 'of'.

out.reply: I understand. It can be difficult to be independent sometimes. Do you work or are you a student?

new_vocab.example: You can rely on me.
I want to earn money to travel.

out.follow_up: Are you studying or working at the moment?

out.corrected_sentence: He suggested that I take a taxi.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese, il verbo 'suggest' non si usa con la struttura 'suggest someone to do something'. Si usa invece 'suggest that someone do something' oppure 'suggest doing something'.

out.reply: That was a good idea! Taxis can be very convenient when you are in a hurry.

new_vocab.example: I am in a hurry to catch the train.
The supermarket is very convenient because it is near my house.

out.follow_up: Do you usually prefer taking a taxi or using public transport?

out.corrected_sentence: I have a lot of information about this city.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese la parola 'information' è un nome non numerabile, quindi non si usa mai al plurale.

out.reply: That is great! What is the most interesting thing about this city?

new_vocab.example: I love going sightseeing when I visit a new city.

out.follow_up: Can you tell me one interesting place to visit there?

out.corrected_sentence: I have been working in this company since 2019.

corrections.explanation_it: Quando parli di un'azione che è iniziata nel passato e continua ancora nel presente, devi usare il Present Perfect Continuous.

out.reply: That is a long time! Do you enjoy your job there?

new_vocab.example: It is a long-term project.

out.follow_up: What is your main responsibility at work?

out.corrected_sentence: Everybody is welcome to join us.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese, i pronomi indefiniti come 'everybody' o 'everyone' sono sempre singolari e richiedono il verbo al singolare.

out.reply: That is a very kind invitation! Are you planning a special event or a party soon?

new_vocab.example: Are you going to host a party next week?

out.follow_up: Can you tell me more about the event you are planning?

out.corrected_sentence: The film was very interesting and we enjoyed it.

corrections.explanation_it: In inglese non si usa 'very much' prima di un aggettivo come 'interesting'. Si usa solo 'very'.
Il verbo 'enjoy' è transitivo e richiede un oggetto. Devi aggiungere 'it' per riferirti al film.

out.reply: That sounds like a great movie! What kind of films do you usually like to watch?

new_vocab.example: The plot of the movie was very exciting.
The cast was amazing.

out.follow_up: Can you tell me more about the plot of the film?

out.corrected_sentence: I've been living here for two years and I really like it.
out.reply: That sounds wonderful! What is your favorite thing about the place where you live?

new_vocab.example: My neighborhood is very quiet and friendly.

out.follow_up: Can you tell me more about your city?

out.corrected_sentence: If I had more time, I would learn another language.
out.reply: That is a great goal to have. Which language would you like to learn if you had the chance?

new_vocab.example: I hope to have a chance to travel to London next year.

out.follow_up: Can you tell me why you want to improve your English?

out.corrected_sentence: She suggested that we take the early train.
out.reply: That sounds like a great idea. Do you usually prefer traveling early in the morning?

new_vocab.example: I need to catch the early train to arrive on time.

out.follow_up: Do you like traveling by train?

out.corrected_sentence: Nobody told me about the meeting, so I missed it.
out.reply: I am sorry to hear that! It is always frustrating when you miss important information. Do you have to attend another meeting later today?

new_vocab.term: to be kept in the loop
new_vocab.example: Please keep me in the loop about the new project.

out.corrected_sentence: so yesterday i was talking with my friend about the trip and we decided to go to spain in august
out.reply: That sounds like a wonderful plan! Spain is beautiful in the summer. Which cities are you planning to visit?

new_vocab.example: I am looking forward to my trip to Spain!

out.follow_up: Tell me more about your trip! What do you want to do there?

out.corrected_sentence: do you know where i can find a good restaurant near here
out.reply: I am not sure where you are right now, but I can help you practice how to ask for recommendations. What kind of food do you like to eat?

new_vocab.example: Can you give me a restaurant recommendation?
Is there a pharmacy nearby?

out.follow_up: Tell me, do you prefer Italian food or international food?

out.corrected_sentence: I installed Llama on my MacBook and now I'm testing German with FastAPI and React.
out.reply: That sounds like a very interesting technical project! Are you learning German for work or just for fun?

new_vocab.example: I need to set up my new development environment.
Learning a new programming language can be challenging.

out.follow_up: Can you tell me more about why you are using React for this project?

out.corrected_sentence: Ciao, non so come si dice in inglese: vorrei prenotare una camera per due notti.
out.reply: In English, you can say: I would like to book a room for two nights. Can you try saying that?

new_vocab.example: I need to book a flight to London.
Is there a room available for tonight?

out.follow_up: Try to repeat the sentence: I would like to book a room for two nights.
